chunks: "An LDO's efficiency is about Vout over Vin, so it can only compete when the drop is small.
The break-even is simple: the LDO is more efficient if Vout over Vin is greater than the buck's efficiency. If a buck is 90 percent, that's anything above about 3.
67 volts in for 3. 3 out, so 3. 6 volts to 3. 3 volts gives the LDO 92 percent. The other case is very light load.
A buck has fixed overhead: the controller's quiescent current, gate drive, a bit of switching loss every cycle.
If the load is, say, 10 microamps, that overhead can be bigger than the load itself, and a nano-power LDO with one microamp of Iq can beat it.
Of course an LDO also has quiescent current, so it depends on the numbers. But a big drop is a big drop. At 12 to 3. 3 volts at any serious current the LDO is hopeless.
And the LDO has other reasons to win that aren't efficiency: no inductor, no switching noise, less area."
